title: Day-of Rollout: staffing checklist and telemetry anchor (Dec 2026) - notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, day-of-rollout pocket checklist and telemetry anchor for the Dec 2026 rollout window. Intended for quick consumption by the deployment conductor and on-call engineers. Focus is staffing, short timelines, key telemetry probes, and an editable release-notes sketch for post-flight.

Scope:
- Applies to: hosted API and Dedicated routing changes for model-routing fallback feature (partial traffic shifts).
- Excludes: Private on-prem packaging (handled separately).
- Traffic pattern: gradual 0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3 hours with hold windows.

Quick commander notes (TL;DR):
- Conductor: Priya Patel (primary), backup: Ethan Cho
- Start window: 2026-12-10 09:00 PT (preflight), go/no-go at 10:15 PT, gradual ramp begins 10:30 PT
- Communication channel: #deploys (urgent thread pinned) + PagerDuty escalation policy (Release Conductor)
- Abort triggers: >3xx spike > 1% above baseline sustained for 5 minutes; p50 latency increase >30% for 3 consecutive minutes; CPU/GPU saturation on any Dedicated node >85% for 10 mins.

Preflight checklist (48h -> 1h before):
- 48h: confirm canary metrics baseline (observability owner: Ava) and synthetic test pass rate >= 98%
- 24h: finalize config pins and rollback image tags in k8s manifests and Dedicated pool (PR #4982 merged)
- 12h: confirm capacity reservations (Dedicated) and burst lanes configured; confirm autoscaler policies (infra owner: Liam)
- 6h: ensure runbook printed/pinned to drive and offline copies with operators on-call
- 2h: run smoke suite against staging (end-to-end traces), verify no new regressions in generation quality evals
- 30m: badge check: all required staff present in call; Slack status set to "on-release"; validate synthetic heartbeat monitors
- 5m: quick warm-up: pre-warm model instances with representative prompts on 3 regions

Day-of staffing roster (hour blocks):
- Conductor (overall decision): Priya Patel (09:00-13:00)
- Observability lead: Ava Martinez (08:30-14:00) -> responsible for dashboards and signal gating
- Infra lead (scaling/VMs): Liam O'Connor (08:30-12:30)
- Serving runtime SME: Maya Singh (09:00-13:00)
- Release engineer (deploy actions): Ethan Cho (09:00-11:00), backup: Sasha Rivera (11:00-14:00)
- Customer Success standby (for priority customers): Jordan Lee (10:00-14:00)
- Nightwatch secondary (post 14:00 handoff): On-call SRE rotation (PD: #sre-release)

Short contact cheatsheet:
- Conductor PD: +1-555-1212 (priority), Slack: @priya
- Observability PD: +1-555-1313, Slack: @ava
- Infra PD: +1-555-1414, Slack: @liam
- Serving runtime: Slack: @maya
- Release engineer: Slack: @ethan

Rollout calendar (minute-level anchors):
- 09:00 PT: Preflight call (15m) - confirm baselines, final go/no-go pollers, confirm smoke test signatures.
- 09:20 PT: Run synthetic smoke suite (10m) and surface key metrics on rollcall dashboard.
- 09:35 PT: Finalize and freeze deploy artifacts: image manifest, routing rules, rollout plan in k8s rollout CR.
- 10:00 PT: 20m dry run (internal traffic only) - exercise fallback logic and KV cache invalidation.
- 10:20 PT: Go/No-Go poll; capture decisions in release-conductor doc. If no-go, immediate abort to rollback tag and abort communications.
- 10:30 PT: 1% traffic shift (hold 15m) - monitor for errors and latency, Observability to post p95/p99 and errors to Slack every 5m.
- 10:45 PT: decision checkpoint: if good, shift to 5% (hold 20m) else rollback to 0% and open incident if unstable.
- 11:05 PT: shift to 25% (hold 30m) - watch throughput and KV cache effectiveness.
- 11:35 PT: shift to 100% (ramp over 10m) - continuous checks for 60m.
- 12:45 PT: start cool-down and prepare post-release notes and telemetry digest.

Telemetry anchor (signals to watch, short descriptions):
- API surface: 5xx rate by endpoint (alerts at +0.5% absolute rise), 4xx anomalies (config errors), p50/p95/p99 latencies (per region), tail-latency drift (>30% relative from baseline)
- Cost/throughput: tokens/sec per instance and inference-costs estimate (approx. delta vs baseline)
- Resource: GPU util, mem pressure, OOM events on dedicated hosts
- Model quality: regression probes (top-5 prompt set from evals), BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies and human-feedback counts from CS triage
- Cache effectiveness: KV hit ratio and token saving delta (expect >12% for common prefixes)
- Fallbacks: # of automatic fallbacks triggered and success rate (target <0.2% autoswitch)

Dashboard checklist (observability owner):
- Rollout overview: quickchart showing percentage traffic, errors, latencies, and region split
- Heatmap: 30m sliding window of p99 by model shard
- Canary diff: side-by-side of metrics for old vs new variant for the same route
- Synthetic runner: pass/fail counts and latency trend
- Incident links: pinned incident templates and runbooks

Abort and rollback decision matrix (simple):
- Immediate abort (rollback to 0%): sustained 5xx spike (>1% above baseline) for 5m OR p99 latency >2x baseline for 5m OR critical customer P1 reported and reproducible
- Soft hold (pause on current %): any single signal breach (latency or error) lasting <5m; escalate to infra/serving SME and observe for next hold window
- Partial rollback to prior percentage (e.g., 25% -> 5%): repeated transient spikes that resolve with lower traffic and indicate load-related degradation

Rollback steps (fast rollback):
- Conductor authorizes rollback on call (explicit phrase: "ROLLBACK NOW")
- Release engineer triggers k8s rollout revert to previous image tag and routing change to previous variant (runbook command snippet: ./scripts/rollback-to-tag.sh v1234)
- Observability to mark timeline and add alert annotations
- Notify CS and PagerDuty: incident created, affected customers listed, postmortem owner assigned

Communications (what to say, channels):
- Slack: #deploys (short bullets every checkpoint), #customers (summary if customer-affect), email: release-notes-digest@redwood.io for long form
- Customer message template: brief summary, expected impact, mitigation steps, customer support contact
- Internal template: timeline, metrics observed, decision rationale, owners for follow-ups

Post-release notes (post 60–120m stability window):
- Short summary: what shipped (model-routing fallback v1), target segments, expected improvements (latency tail reduction, cost savings)
- High-level metrics: delta p95, error-rate delta, token-cost delta, KV hit ratio change
- Known issues: anything observed during rollout (list) and temporary workarounds
- Action items: follow-ups with owners and due dates (e.g., "tune autoscaler - Liam - due 2026-12-20")
- Links: PRs, dashboards, incident if any, and retro doc

Release-notes skeleton (to paste into GH release or product-notes):
- Title: model-routing fallback v1 (Dec 2026)
- Summary: Adds an automated fallback path for model routing to improve reliability under overload conditions and reduce costly token retries. Deploying gradually with telemetry gating.
- Impact: expected lower error rate during overload, slight initial rollout risk for edge KV cache mismatches.
- Rollout plan: gradual ramp across regions; full rollout by 12:00 PT on 2026-12-10 if stable.
- Revert plan: immediate rollback to previous routing variant on operator signal.

Backlog / open questions (notes to self):
- Double-check whether Dedicated autoscaler has per-model cooldown independent of global pool (Ticket INF-4521).
- Need a short-run synthetic that exercises multi-tenant KV eviction behavior (Maya to prototype).
- Confirm whether cost delta reporting needs a new tag in billing pipeline (Finance/Cost team to sign off).
- Should we include a short client-side retry-circuit sample to reduce visible 4xx while fallback warms? (CS suggestion)

Post-mortem / retro hooks (if incident):
- If we hit an incident, capture timeline within 30 mins post rollback, assign PM and Eng lead for fix, schedule retro within 3 working days, and link JIRA with postmortem template.

Notes to operators (tips):
- If you see a p50 shift but no 5xx, prefer to hold and observe (latency tuning often not binary).
- When rolling back, annotate the exact rollout percentage and timestamp in the Jira and Slack messages to avoid confusion.
- Keep the synthetic runner running for at least 60m post-100% to catch slow-burning regressions.

Appendix: quick command cheats (internal):
- preview rollout status: ./ctl rollout status --env=prod --route=model-routing
- force rollback: ./ctl rollout revert --to-tag=v1234 --route=model-routing
- scale dedicated pool: ./infra scale-pool --pool=dedicated-model-3 --replicas=12
- collect traces: ./obs collect --from=2026-12-10T10:30:00Z --duration=PT1H --service=model-serving

Scratch area (for scribbles during call):
- 09:02: baseline p99: 320ms region-us-west-2
- 09:22 synthetic fail: 4/50 flakiness on prompt set B (investigate prefix caching)
- 10:33 1% shift: p99 -> 410ms (+28%), 5xx+0.3% -> HOLD
- 10:40 quick fix attempted: warm cache; success indicator: KV hit ratio +4% -> decision to continue to 5%
- 11:10 25% shift: GPU util 78% on shard-5 (watch)

End of doc.

(Internal: keep this as the working pocket doc; final runbook to be migrated to Confluence after the rollout completes.)
